references.text: Exhortation to keep all that the Lord has commanded, without adding or taking away
Command to fear the Lord alone and not follow other gods
Warning against seeking after the gods of other peoples and their ways of worship
Joshua's exhortation not to mention the names of foreign gods, swear by them, or serve them
Those who follow other gods bring much sorrow; David will not take their names upon his lips
The Lord will remove the names of Baal from Israel's mouth, so they are no longer remembered
Prophecy that the names of idols shall be wiped out from the land and no longer remembered
Paul exhorts believers that idolatry should not even be mentioned among them
Deuteronomy 4:2 and 13:1 expand on the requirement for unchanging obedience by specifying the prohibition against altering God's word.
Deuteronomy 4:2 confirms and clarifies the requirement to keep God's word without change, as a direct response to the message in Exodus.
2 Kings 17:37 directly links keeping God's commands with the prohibition against fearing other gods, just as in Exodus.
Jeremiah 25:6 confirms and applies the prohibition against turning to other gods, which is central to Exodus 23:13.
2 Kings 17:38 emphasizes that the covenant requires rejection of other gods, a direct parallel to Exodus' warning.
Deuteronomy 28:14 directly links keeping God's word with the prohibition against following other gods.
